Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: The Protection of Personal Data Law was enacted on 29 June 2021, establishing a comprehensive GDPR-aligned data protection framework. It mandates consent, transparency, data subject rights, security measures, data breach notification, and DPO appointment for public authorities.
revision_notes: Cited sources (techhiveadvisory, lawgratis) give inconsistent dates (2021 vs 2019) for enactment and neither cites a law number or promulgation decree. The official Ministry of Justice legal database hosts only the Assembly-adopted 2014 text (Loi n°14-029/AU, delibérée 26 June 2014) with no promulgation decree, unlike comparable Comorian laws which explicitly show a décret de promulgation. Data Protection Africa's factsheet (updated May 2022) states 'NO DATA PROTECTION LAW' and a November 2023 Internews/ARISA legal-environment review confirms the 2014 draft 'does not appear to have been enacted' and that Comoros has no dedicated data protection law or authority. The 29 June 2021 date used by techhiveadvisory coincides with an unrelated Comorian foreign-trade law (Loi n°21-013/AU), suggesting a sourcing error. Revised down to 1 (No) on balance of evidence, but flagged for human review given conflicting claims and no located 2024-2026 update.
revised_comments: Comoros has not enacted a dedicated data protection law. A draft Personal Data Protection bill (Loi n°14-029/AU) was adopted by the Assembly of the Union on 26 June 2014, but no presidential decree promulgating it has been issued, unlike other Comorian legislation which typically requires such a decree to take legal effect. As of the most recent assessments (Data Protection Africa, 2022; Internews/ARISA legal environment review, 2023), Comoros has no operative data protection legislation and no data protection authority has been established.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The biometric national ID card is the recognised legal proof of identity for voting, accessing public services, and legal/financial transactions. The 2023 Electoral Code explicitly lists the biometric national ID as an accepted identity document for voter registration.
revision_notes: Score confirmed but Year corrected: the digital (biometric) ID law (Loi n°14-023/AU) was adopted by the Assembly in 2014 but only formally promulgated by Décret n°14-137/PR on 28 August 2024, which is when it took legal effect. The 2023 Electoral Code (Code électoral 2023, justice.gouv.km) confirms a valid biometric identity document is required for voter registration/verification. Original sources (Wikipedia, Smile ID) were generic but the underlying claim checks out against primary legal texts.
revised_comments: The Comorian biometric national identity card is legally recognised as proof of identity. Presidential Decree n°14-137/PR of 28 August 2024 promulgated Law n°14-023/AU of 24 June 2014, which establishes the digital (biometric) national identity card, giving it formal legal effect. The 2023 Electoral Code requires a valid biometric national identity document for voter registration and permits its use to vote in place of a lost voter card. The longstanding 1987 identity card law (Loi n°87-012) similarly obliges all residents aged 18 and above to be able to prove their identity at all times.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: Law n°14-023/AU of 24 June 2014 establishing the Comorian digital (biometric) national identity card provides the legal framework. Promulgated by Decree n°14-137/PR on 28 August 2024. The 2023 Electoral Code also references the biometric national ID card.
revision_notes: Score confirmed. Year corrected from 2014 to 2024: the law was adopted by the Assembly of the Union on 24 June 2014 but only took legal effect once promulgated by Décret n°14-137/PR on 28 August 2024 (fetched and confirmed on justice.gouv.km). Comments already noted this decree; the Year field is updated to match the vintage of the operative legal instrument.
revised_comments: Formal legislation governs the Comorian digital identity system. Law n°14-023/AU, adopted by the Assembly of the Union on 24 June 2014, establishes the digital (biometric) national identity card. It was formally promulgated by Presidential Decree n°14-137/PR on 28 August 2024, giving it legal force. The 2023 Electoral Code also references the biometric national identity card as an accepted identity document.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: The Comorian biometric national ID card collects fingerprints. Biometric enrollment has been managed by Semlex (Belgium) and transitioning to Genkey (Netherlands) from April 2026. No evidence of iris/facial biometrics in the national ID system.
revision_notes: The World Bank ID4D 'State of Identification Systems in Africa' country profile states enrollment for the Comorian NID captures all 10 fingerprints AND a digital photograph (facial image), i.e. more than 'fingerprints only'. This is a recommended primary source per the metadata guidelines. However the ID4D profile dates from 2017 and it is not certain whether the photograph is used as a biometric (facial-recognition) modality versus a plain ID photo, and no dedicated confirmation of iris or facial-recognition biometrics was found for the current Semlex/GenKey system. Proposed upgrade to 3 (Facial/Iris) is tentative and flagged for human review rather than asserted outright.
revised_comments: The Comorian biometric national identity system collects fingerprints and a facial image (digital photograph) at enrolment. World Bank ID4D documentation describes capture of all 10 fingerprints together with a digital photograph as part of the standard enrolment process, managed historically by Semlex (Belgium) and transitioning to GenKey (Netherlands) from April 2026, with biometric data increasingly domiciled within Comoros.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: Biometric data is collected and stored digitally. The Central Service for the Production and Issuance of Biometric Documents manages digital records. Biometric data was domiciled in Belgium under Semlex; transitioning to in-country domiciliation under Genkey from 2026.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Recent (2026) reporting on the Semlex-to-GenKey transition confirms identity records remain fully digital/biometric, with data now being domiciled within Comoros rather than Belgium, consistent with the existing score of 3 (Digital).
revised_comments: Comorian identity records are held in fully electronic/digital format. Biometric enrolment data has historically been produced and stored under a build-operate-transfer arrangement with Semlex (Belgium); from April 2026 GenKey (Netherlands) takes over production, with biometric data to be domiciled within Comoros rather than abroad, maintaining a fully digital record-keeping system.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: The Comorian biometric national ID card is mandatory for all nationals from age 18. Wikipedia and Smile ID confirm compulsory enrollment at age 18.
revision_notes: Confirmed against the primary legal text: Loi n°87-012 (1 August 1987), Article 1, requires every person aged 18 («dix-huit ans accomplie») resident in Comoros to be able to prove their identity, and this remains the operative age threshold per an August 2025 government enforcement announcement on mandatory ID-carrying. Original Wikipedia/Smile ID sources were weak but the underlying figure is correct.
revised_comments: Comorian nationals become eligible, and are required, to hold a national identity card from age 18. This threshold derives from Loi n°87-012 of 1 August 1987 governing the national identity card, and was reaffirmed by an August 2025 government announcement making it mandatory for all Comorians to carry and present their identity card.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: The Comorian national identity card is compulsory for all Comorian nationals (mandatory for all).
revision_notes: Confirmed. Loi n°87-012 (1987) obliges every resident aged 18+ to be able to prove their identity via the national card, and an August 2025 Ministry of Interior announcement made carrying and presenting the card compulsory for all Comorians, with checks on minors and foreigners handled differently. This supports 'mandatory for all' status.
revised_comments: Registration for, and possession of, the Comorian national identity card is mandatory for all citizens from age 18, under Loi n°87-012 of 1987. Enforcement was reinforced in August 2025 when the Ministry of the Interior made it compulsory for all Comorians to carry and present their national identity card during checks.
